chunks.doc_title: Northwind Systems Ltd — Amendment No. 1 to the Master Services Agreement
chunks.text:
This Amendment No. 1 is entered into on 18 November 2024 and amends the Master Services
Agreement dated 1 April 2023 (MAT-NW-MSA-2023). Where this Amendment conflicts with the
original Agreement, this Amendment prevails.

chunks.doc_title: Northwind Systems Ltd — Amendment No. 1 to the Master Services Agreement
chunks.text:
Clause 14.3 of the Agreement is deleted in its entirety and replaced with:

"14.3 The Supplier's aggregate liability under the indemnity at clause 15 shall be capped
at **GBP 5,000,000** per contract year. This cap shall survive termination or expiry of
this Agreement for a period of six years."

**Effect:** the indemnity cap is raised from GBP 2,000,000 to GBP 5,000,000, and — unlike
the original drafting — it now expressly survives termination for six years.

Any statement that the indemnity cap is GBP 2,000,000, or that clause 14 does not survive
termination, is describing the superseded 2023 text and is stale as of 18 November 2024.

chunks.doc_title: Northwind Systems Ltd — Amendment No. 1 to the Master Services Agreement
chunks.text:
Clause 22.4 is amended to add clause 14 (Limitation of liability) to the list of surviving
clauses, consistent with the amended clause 14.3 above.

chunks.text:

chunks.doc_title: Northwind Systems Ltd — records retention policy
chunks.text:
Where an automated system produces an assessment relied upon in a decision, the record must
retain: the input, the output, the evidence consulted, the verdict, the identity of the
decision rule applied, and a tamper-evident signature over the assessment.

Records must be reproducible on request within five working days.

chunks.doc_title: Machine learning — dated milestones
chunks.text:
The term "artificial intelligence" was coined for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project of
1956. The perceptron was described by Frank Rosenblatt in 1958.

Backpropagation was popularised for neural networks by Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams in a
1986 Nature paper. AlexNet won the ImageNet competition in 2012, and is generally taken as
the start of the modern deep learning era.

The transformer architecture was introduced in "Attention Is All You Need" by Vaswani et
al. at NeurIPS in 2017. BERT followed in 2018.

chunks.doc_title: Machine learning — dated milestones
chunks.text:
Reported accuracy figures are meaningful only against a named dataset, split and metric. A
bare percentage with no dataset attached is not a verifiable claim.

chunks.doc_title: Machine learning — dated milestones
chunks.text:
In the language-model literature, "hallucination" refers to fluent output that is not
grounded in the model's inputs or in fact. Surveys consistently find that expressed
confidence in model output correlates poorly with factual accuracy, which is why
confidence stated in prose cannot be used as evidence of correctness.

chunks.doc_title: Classic animated series — studio attribution
chunks.text:
Tom and Jerry was created by William Hanna and Joseph Barbera and produced by
**Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer**, debuting with "Puss Gets the Boot" in 1940. It is not a Disney
production and never has been. MGM's animation unit produced the original theatrical
shorts through 1958; later entries were made by Hanna-Barbera, Chuck Jones's unit, and
subsequently Warner Bros., which holds the rights today.

Attributing Tom and Jerry to Disney is a studio misattribution.

chunks.doc_title: Classic animated series — studio attribution
chunks.text:
Disney's own early features include Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937), Pinocchio
(1940), Fantasia (1940) and Dumbo (1941). Disney's flagship shorts character is Mickey
Mouse, introduced in Steamboat Willie in 1928.

chunks.doc_title: Classic animated series — studio attribution
chunks.text:
Looney Tunes and Merrie Melodies, featuring Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, were produced by
Warner Bros., not Disney or MGM.

chunks.doc_title: Eiffel Tower — structural and historical record
chunks.text:
The Eiffel Tower was designed and built by the engineering company of Gustave Eiffel.
Construction began in January 1887 and the tower was completed in March 1889. It was
inaugurated on 31 March 1889. Napoleon Bonaparte, who died in 1821, had no involvement in
its design, construction or commissioning.

The tower was erected as the entrance arch to the 1889 Exposition Universelle, a world's
fair held in Paris to mark the centenary of the French Revolution of 1789. The date 1789
therefore appears in the tower's history as the event being commemorated, not as the year
of construction — a distinction that is commonly collapsed in error.

chunks.doc_title: Eiffel Tower — structural and historical record
chunks.text:
As completed in 1889 the tower stood 300 metres tall. With the broadcast aerials added
later its total height is 330 metres. It was the tallest man-made structure in the world
from 1889 until 1930, when the Chrysler Building in New York surpassed it.

At 330 metres the Eiffel Tower is not the tallest structure in Europe and has not been for
decades. See REF-TALLEST-01 for the current European and world records.

chunks.doc_title: Eiffel Tower — structural and historical record
chunks.text:
The detailed design work was carried out by Maurice Koechlin and Émile Nouguier, engineers
at Eiffel's company, with architectural contributions from Stephen Sauvestre. Gustave
Eiffel purchased the rights to the design and the tower carries his name.

chunks.doc_title: FIFA World Cup — tournament and winners record
chunks.text:
The FIFA World Cup is held every four years. Winners of recent tournaments:

- 2006 — Italy
- 2010 — Spain
- 2014 — Germany
- 2018 — France
- 2022 — Argentina, defeating France on penalties in Qatar

chunks.doc_title: FIFA World Cup — tournament and winners record
chunks.text:
The 2026 tournament is hosted jointly by Canada, Mexico and the United States and is the
first to feature 48 teams.

There is no FIFA World Cup scheduled for 2027. The tournament runs on a four-year cycle,
so the edition following 2026 is scheduled for 2030. As of the effective date of this
record, no tournament after 2022 has been completed, and therefore **no winner exists for
any tournament dated 2026 or later.**

Any statement naming a winner of a World Cup dated 2027 refers to a tournament that is not
scheduled to exist. Any statement naming a winner of a tournament dated after the present
day describes an event that has not occurred.

chunks.doc_title: FIFA World Cup — tournament and winners record
chunks.text:
Brazil has won the most titles with five. Germany and Italy have four each. Argentina has
three, the most recent in 2022.

chunks.doc_title: Nobel Prizes — categories and award rules
chunks.text:
Nobel Prizes are awarded in exactly six categories: Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or
Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economic Sciences. The first five were established by
Alfred Nobel's will of 1895; the Economic Sciences prize was established by Sweden's
central bank in 1968 and is formally the Sveriges Riksbank Prize.

**There is no Nobel Prize in Quantum Computing, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering
or Biology.** Work in quantum information has been recognised under the Physics prize —
the 2022 Physics prize was awarded for experiments with entangled photons — but no
category by that name exists or has ever existed.

chunks.doc_title: Nobel Prizes — categories and award rules
chunks.text:
Prizes are announced in early October each year and presented on 10 December, the
anniversary of Nobel's death. Awards are never announced for future years.

Any statement describing a Nobel Prize awarded in a year later than the present date
describes an award that has not been made. Any statement naming a Nobel Prize category
outside the six listed above describes a prize that does not exist.

chunks.doc_title: Nobel Prizes — categories and award rules
chunks.text:
A prize in the sciences may be shared by at most three laureates. Prizes are not awarded
posthumously, except where a laureate dies after the announcement. Nominations remain
sealed for fifty years.

chunks.doc_title: Photosynthesis — process summary
chunks.text:
Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, algae and some bacteria convert light
energy into chemical energy stored as carbohydrates. Carbon dioxide and water are consumed
and oxygen is released as a by-product.

The overall balanced equation is six molecules of carbon dioxide plus six molecules of
water, driven by light energy, yielding one molecule of glucose and six molecules of
oxygen.

chunks.doc_title: Photosynthesis — process summary
chunks.text:
In plants the process takes place in the chloroplasts, organelles containing the green
pigment chlorophyll. Chlorophyll absorbs light most strongly in the blue and red parts of
the visible spectrum and reflects green light, which is why foliage appears green.

chunks.doc_title: Photosynthesis — process summary
chunks.text:
The light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes. Light energy splits water,
releasing oxygen and generating ATP and NADPH.

The light-independent reactions, known as the Calvin cycle, occur in the stroma. They use
the ATP and NADPH produced in the first stage to fix carbon dioxide into three-carbon
sugars, which are assembled into glucose.

chunks.doc_title: Photosynthesis — process summary
chunks.text:
Photosynthesis is the primary route by which energy enters most food webs, and it is the
origin of the oxygen in Earth's atmosphere.

chunks.doc_title: Crewed spaceflight — milestone record
chunks.text:
Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space aboard Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961. Alan
Shepard followed on 5 May 1961. Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space aboard
Vostok 6 in June 1963.

chunks.doc_title: Crewed spaceflight — milestone record
chunks.text:
Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the
surface while Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit. Six Apollo missions landed
successfully — Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16 and 17 — placing twelve people on the surface in
total. Apollo 13 suffered an oxygen tank failure and returned without landing.

The last crewed lunar landing was Apollo 17 in December 1972. No crewed landing has taken
place since.

chunks.doc_title: Crewed spaceflight — milestone record
chunks.text:
No human has travelled to Mars. All Mars missions to date have been robotic. Any statement
describing a completed crewed Mars landing describes an event that has not occurred.

chunks.doc_title: Tallest buildings and structures — current records
chunks.text:
The Burj Khalifa in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, is the tallest building and the tallest
free-standing structure in the world at 828 metres, completed in 2010. It is emphatically
not the shortest tower by any measure; among notable towers worldwide it ranks first by
height.

The Merdeka 118 tower in Kuala Lumpur is the second tallest building at 679 metres.

chunks.doc_title: Tallest buildings and structures — current records
chunks.text:
The tallest structure in Europe is the Lakhta Center in Saint Petersburg, Russia, at 462
metres, completed in 2019. The tallest structure in the European Union is the Varso Tower
in Warsaw, Poland, at 310 metres including its spire.

No structure in Europe exceeds 500 metres. Any claim that a European structure stands at
over 500 metres is inconsistent with the current record.

chunks.doc_title: Tallest buildings and structures — current records
chunks.text:
The Eiffel Tower, at 330 metres including aerials, is materially shorter than the Lakhta
Center and roughly 40 percent of the height of the Burj Khalifa. It held the world record
between 1889 and 1930 only.

chunks.doc_title: Invention of the telephone — patent record
chunks.text:
Alexander Graham Bell was granted US Patent 174,465 for the telephone on 7 March 1876,
having filed on 14 February 1876. Bell demonstrated speech transmission to his assistant
Thomas Watson on 10 March 1876.

Bell founded the Bell Telephone Company in 1877.

chunks.doc_title: Invention of the telephone — patent record
chunks.text:
Elisha Gray filed a caveat describing a similar liquid transmitter on the same day Bell
filed his application, producing one of the most litigated priority disputes in patent
history.

Antonio Meucci demonstrated a voice-transmitting device in the 1850s and filed a caveat in
1871 that he did not renew. In 2002 the US House of Representatives passed a resolution
recognising Meucci's contribution. Johann Philipp Reis built an earlier device that
transmitted tone but not intelligible speech.

The attribution of the telephone to Bell is therefore correct as a matter of the 1876
patent record, while the broader question of first invention remains contested.

chunks.doc_title: Physical geography — superlatives
chunks.text:
Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level at 8,849 metres, on the border of
Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. The 8,849-metre figure comes from the joint
Nepal–China survey published in December 2020, revising the earlier 8,848-metre value.

K2 is the second highest at 8,611 metres. Mauna Kea is taller measured from its base on the
sea floor, but not above sea level.

chunks.doc_title: Physical geography — superlatives
chunks.text:
The Nile and the Amazon are the two longest rivers, and which ranks first depends on where
the Amazon's source is taken to be; the Nile is conventionally cited at about 6,650 km. The
Amazon carries by far the greatest volume of water.

The Sahara is the largest hot desert at about 9.2 million square kilometres. Antarctica is
the largest desert of any kind.

chunks.doc_title: Physical geography — superlatives
chunks.text:
The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean. Its deepest point, Challenger Deep in the
Mariana Trench, is approximately 10,935 metres below sea level.
